nodes.label: Audit Verdict: Cryptographically Sound — Not Crackable in Any Practical Sense
nodes.rationale: Every roll mixes a fresh 256-bit kernel-CSPRNG secret with independent node randomness through SHA3, with exact rejection sampling. An attacker faces 2^128–2^256 uniform possibilities and no computational shortcut; the weak-PRNG failure class behind the wallet-drain hacks does not exist in this design.
nodes.norm_label: audit verdict: cryptographically sound — not crackable in any practical sense
nodes.community_name: Weak-PRNG Wallet-drain Failure Class (small enumerable seed space)

nodes.label: Die-face Pipeline (RollEngine.java, a→b→h→n→face)
nodes.rationale: Ported from the Zero Edge Casino resolve maths, proven on-chain: node random (a), fresh 32-byte SecureRandom secret per roll (b), node computes SHA3(a ++ b) (h), first 4 hash bytes rejection-sampled (n), n mod 6 + 1 is the face.
nodes.community_name: Weak-PRNG Wallet-drain Failure Class (small enumerable seed space)

nodes.label: Dual Independent Entropy Sources (node CSPRNG + Android kernel CSPRNG)
nodes.rationale: Two independent CSPRNGs are mixed so that either source alone failing still leaves the output unpredictable: the Minima node's random command plus a fresh per-roll 32-byte SecureRandom secret that nobody else ever sees in advance.
nodes.norm_label: dual independent entropy sources (node csprng + android kernel csprng)
nodes.community_name: Weak-PRNG Wallet-drain Failure Class (small enumerable seed space)

nodes.label: SHA3 Node-side Mixing, Bit-identical to KISS VM (runscript re-verification)
nodes.rationale: The node computes SHA3(a ++ b) bit-identically to the KISS VM script so any roll can be re-verified with runscript in a Minima terminal. Running SHA3 on the node is the deliberate price of on-chain verifiability — the node necessarily sees both secrets.
nodes.norm_label: sha3 node-side mixing, bit-identical to kiss vm (runscript re-verification)
nodes.community_name: Weak-PRNG Wallet-drain Failure Class (small enumerable seed space)

nodes.label: Exact Rejection Sampling (threshold 4294967292 = floor(2^32/6)·6)
nodes.rationale: Values ≥ 4294967292 are rerolled so every face is exactly 1/6 — zero modulo bias, pinned by the Bip39Test.rejectionThresholdIsExact unit test; errors out after 25 rejects rather than degrade.
nodes.community_name: Weak-PRNG Wallet-drain Failure Class (small enumerable seed space)

nodes.label: iancoleman Unbiased Dice Encoding (faces→bits→words, self-test gated)
nodes.rationale: Faces become entropy bits via the iancoleman unbiased encoding with raw truncation; Bip39Test verifies parity with iancoleman/bip39 v0.4.3 and Bip39.selfTest() blocks generation entirely if the self-test fails.

nodes.label: Weak-PRNG Wallet-drain Failure Class (small enumerable seed space)
nodes.rationale: Every drained-wallet RNG incident shared one root cause: a non-cryptographic generator seeded with a handful of guessable bits invented the whole seed, letting attackers enumerate every possible seed and sweep the matching addresses. Entropy has no such shortcut — even an adversary who fully controls the node's contribution still faces the 256-bit device secret behind SHA3.

nodes.label: Residual Risk: The Node Can Reconstruct the Seed
nodes.rationale: The SHA3 runs on the node, so Minima Core sees both secrets and hence every face — the deliberate price of on-chain verifiability; if Minima Core or the phone is compromised, any on-device generator has already lost. The per-roll audit log is equally seed-equivalent; 0.1.8 adds a warning above the audit log to treat it exactly like the seed words.

nodes.label: Residual Risk: Demo Mode Lifts FLAG_SECURE
nodes.rationale: Demo mode (0.1.7) makes the screen capturable for presentations; faces captured on a mirrored or recorded screen are seed material. 0.1.8 blocks all rolls — digital and physical — while demo mode is on, and re-blurs any revealed words the moment it is switched on.

nodes.label: Residual Risk: IPC Auth Tokens from java.util.Random
nodes.rationale: The tokens authenticating node replies to the app's exported receiver were minted by a 48-bit-seeded, non-cryptographic PRNG. Blind forgery over broadcasts was already infeasible, but the barrier was thinner than it should be; the shared minimaapi SDK now mints all IPC tokens with SecureRandom.

nodes.label: Digital Rolls vs Five Physical Dice
nodes.rationale: Digital wins on exactness: rejection sampling makes every face exactly 1/6 while household dice carry measurable bias; output is computationally indistinguishable from perfect dice to any adversary who can't break SHA3 or the kernel CSPRNG. Physical wins on unconditional physics, but in this app physical faces are typed into the same phone, so a compromised device reads those too — physical mode only truly wins with the whole derivation done off-device. On an uncompromised phone the digital rolls are at least as strong as ideal dice.
